correctness.rationale: The isolated Fiedler eigenvalue mu=4 sin^2(pi/n) is doubly degenerate. Projection of edge incidence vectors onto its normalized sine/cosine eigenspace has squared norm (8/n)sin^2(pi d/n) and mutual absolute cosine determined by endpoint sums. Degenerate perturbation yields the smaller eigenvalue of H=xpp^T+(1-x)qq^T. The two-vector maximization is ab(1-c^2)/(a+b+2 sqrt(ab)c), with optimal x=(b+sqrt(ab)c)/(a+b+2 sqrt(ab)c). Parity of chord lengths and integer endpoint sums proves each global upper bound and attains it. The 2 mod 4 nonorthogonal upper bound is strictly smaller than the long-short orthogonal gain; for odd n maximal chords realize the closest discrete right angle. The isolated eigenspace and bounded updates give a uniform-in-choice O_n(eps^2) remainder. A rank-one single chord leaves one Fiedler eigenvector unchanged, so no gain. Independent numeric enumeration checked all unordered eligible chord pairs for n=4..17 against formulas, including S_6=4/7; infinite proof is the exact Fourier/parity argument.
residual_risks: Independent computation n<=17 is corroboration, not an all-n proof; all-n proof rests on the inspected parity inequalities.

value.rationale: Finding a cheapest pair of additional consensus links that first lifts a repeated Fiedler eigenvalue is a natural graph-design problem. The all-size closed form, parity-sensitive optimizer, and counterintuitive n=2 mod 4 shorter-chord superiority are exact, potentially reusable benchmarks, beyond a routine perturbation example.
residual_risks: Only infinitesimal conductance is optimized; finite-budget optima can differ.

final_claim: For all n>=4, two nonedge chords of C_n with total conductance eps optimize the linear coefficient of lambda_2 exactly by three congruence cases: odd n: 4/n cos^2(pi/(2n))(1-sin(pi/(2n))); n divisible by four: 4/n; n=2 mod 4: (8/n) cos^2(pi/n)/(1+cos^2(pi/n)). In the third case the optimal orthogonal chords are a diameter and a length-n/2-1 chord with the shorter chord receiving the larger conductance share. Any one chord leaves lambda_2 unchanged.
limitations: n>=4 only; unweighted undirected cycles, nonedge distinct chords, equal edge-conductance prices, epsilon->0.
No claim that the same pair optimizes a fixed non-small conductance budget.
